posts.text:
Everyone chasing outbound thinks the game is volume.
 
More sends. More clicks. More reach.
 
I used to think that too.
 
Then I saw the numbers behind who actually converts on a tool I've been recommending.
 
One affiliate brought in 2 paying customers from 2 clicks.
 
Another brought in 2 customers with zero tracked clicks.
 
Meanwhile, links with hundreds of clicks converted nothing.
 
Here's what separates them:
 
They're not promoting a tool. They're recommending something they already use inside work they're already doing.
 
Cold traffic converts at a fraction of a percent.
 
A client you already have a relationship with? Closer to 1 in 5.
 
Volume was never the lever. Trust was.
 
I've been rethinking how I show up because of this. Less "check out this tool," more "here's what I actually build client processes on."
 
If you're doing outbound and still chasing clicks instead of context, you're solving the wrong problem.
 
Want the tool I've been building my outbound process around?
 
Comment LEMLIST and I'll send it over.

Try this. Ask ChatGPT to recommend a business in your industry.

Now check if yours shows up.

For most businesses, the answer is no. Not because the business is bad. Because AI tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Google's AI results don't know it exists.

This is happening right now, quietly. Customers are asking AI where to go, what to buy, whom to hire, before they even open Google. If your business isn't part of that answer, you're invisible to a growing share of your own market.

The fix isn't complicated. It just hasn't been built into most marketing yet: structured content, FAQ pages, and a footprint AI tools can actually read and recommend from.

This is the gap MABIDO fills.

Whether you're a brand seeking creators who deliver real results or a creator ready to land meaningful partnerships, NaanoX is where it happens.

If you run a business or work with clients (agencies, freelancers, anyone with a website), this matters. 

Either offer it to them, or build it for yourself.

Link to the tool that built Bruno's footprint is in the comments.

I rewrote this outbound email in my head 3 times before I realized the problem wasn't the copy.

Someone sent me this last week:

"Most people aren't serious about LinkedIn. They want the results. Not the work."

Strong open. I kept reading.

Then it fell apart.

𝐒𝐭𝐞𝐩 𝟏: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐡𝐨𝐨𝐤
 "Most people aren't serious about LinkedIn."
 Open rate bait — works. It's provocative, creates an us-vs-them dynamic.
 Problem: it immediately alienates the reader. You're calling your prospect lazy before asking for $99.

𝐒𝐭𝐞𝐩 𝟐: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐞𝐫
 60-minute consultation. $99. Next week.
 Clear. Specific. Good.
 Problem: no trust built before the ask. I don't know who you are. Why are you worth $99 of my hour?

𝐒𝐭𝐞𝐩 𝟑: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐓𝐀
 "Schedule Your Consultation Here."
 Too early. Cold email with zero credibility asking for a calendar booking and money in the same breath.
 Response rate on this? I'd guess under 0.5%.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐟𝐢𝐱:
 One line of social proof before the offer. One result. One name.
 "We helped a B2B founder close 3 clients in 6 weeks using this exact framework."
 New version would convert 3-4x better.

Built a sequence using this diagnosis in Lemlist in under 20 minutes.

Comment "SEQUENCE," and I'll send you the full rebuilt version.
